season.evidence: Stored Jul-Oct (best mid-Jul to early Oct). Web search (Mountaineers Whistler Mountain page and trip reports, Summitpost, mountain-forecast): climbed as an early-season scramble once SR-20 opens, snow-free by summer; histogram of logged ascents spans May-Oct with June/July/Sept busiest. Treated as Jun-Oct.

track.why: Only one route is stored on the peak. Jun 14 2025, summited, round trip from the Rainy Pass PCT North lot (33 m from our pin) to the summit (9 m), following the described line: leave the PCT, climb through timber to a meadow near 6,000 ft, then the ridge and summit scramble. Report says the ridge was snow-free and the stream approach was brushy. Mid-June is 2 weeks before the stored window opens, within tolerance.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Jul 15 2023 summited round trip from the PCT lot (parking-lot start is 394 m from our pin, which is why it fails the 300 m test); same line, no report.
Jun 15 2023, summited, same line, route fully snow-free; ends ~360 m from our pin.
Jul 23 2022 North Ridge: starts from a highway pullout ~1.7 km east (48.513,-120.689) and climbs the north ridge (class 3-4, one rappel); a different route.

facts.text: By mid-June the route is usually clear of snow except small patches in the 6,000 ft meadow, and the summit ridge is dry.
On the upper ridge keep to the left side, where the rock is firmer; the right side is loose.
Crossing over to the stream too high in the forest costs extra bushwhacking; contour at a lower elevation instead.

notes: The North Ridge (Grade II, class 3-4, one short rappel, from a SR-20 pullout near 48.513,-120.689, Jul 2022 track 1975044) looks like a second route that we do not hold on this peak. Trailhead pin matches where tracks start (the PCT lot spans ~400 m of 48.5146-48.5181), so no move.
